surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the use of ozone (O3) as an oxidizing agent in ALD processes, which dissociates into reactive oxygen radicals at 300 °C. These radicals efficiently eliminate ligands from the surface, leading to higher growth rates compared to thermal ALD using water. The process also involves post-deposition annealing in oxygen or ozone to reduce oxygen deficiencies and carbon impurities in the film.
evidence: O3 dissociation into reactive O radicals occurs at 300 °C, and therefore the elimination of ligands from the surface by O radicals is expected to be more efficient than when H2O is used.
